message.content:
The most recent common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Laurasiatheria is a major group of placental mammals that includes the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong). The MRCA of Laurasiatheria lived roughly 90 million years ago, after the split of the major placental mammal lineages but before the diversification of the individual orders.
